page: Amazon Web Services m5.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute resources are supplied by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system exposes 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores using symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing a standardized 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX and AVX-512F vector execution capabilities alongside 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and offers a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps without integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmark evaluations position the instance squarely in the median range for multi-threaded and memory-centric workloads, though single-core compute performance remains modest. Multi-core evaluation via PassMark yields a score of 7621.07, while multi-threaded stress-ng achieves 6758.13. Memory throughput measures 49.54 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 36.88 GB/sec for writes, enabling 6.65 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.94 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Tradeoffs appear in single-threaded tests, where Geekbench single-core (1036.0) and compression routines perform in the lower quartile. Furthermore, running larger CPU-bound inference models such as a 7B parameter LLM yields constrained token generation rates.

With its dedicated hardware provisioning, m5.2xlarge avoids the performance variability common to burstable instance classes. The balance of memory density and dedicated core capacity makes it architecturally efficient for horizontal enterprise tiers that do not demand fast local NVMe disks or discrete accelerators. Typical matching workloads include relational and caching database instances, containerized application clusters, continuous integration build runners, and general-purpose microservice backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.2xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz across 4 physical multithreaded cores, it incorporates AVX-512 instruction support and a 35 MB L3 cache. The platform includes no local disk storage, relying on network-attached volumes, and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network interface without GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier for multi-core throughput, Redis caching operations, and static web serving, while single-core processing and heavier tasks like 7B LLM inference show architectural constraints. The instance provides consistent resource density suited for microservices, mid-sized databases, and continuous integration environments.
